chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Fatima (peace be upon him) performed the Aqeeqa for her two sons, and shaved their heads on the seventh day, and gave in charity the weight of their hair in silver.
And he (peace be upon him) said: And some people used to stain the head of the child with the blood of the Aqeeqa, and my father used to say: That is Shirk (associating partners with God).
ai.seo_question: What did Lady Fatima do for the Aqeeqa of her sons and what is the ruling on staining the head with blood?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the Sunnah of Aqeeqa by detailing Lady Fatima’s (peace be upon her) specific practice for Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn, including the seventh-day shaving and silver charity, which serves as a primary model for Shia jurisprudence. It further highlights Imam al-Baqir’s (peace be upon him) critique of the pre-Islamic custom of anointing the head with blood, distinguishing it as Shirk and reinforcing the purification of ritual practices. This narration underscores the continuity of prophetic traditions within the Ahl al-Bayt and their role in refining communal worship.
